text: The bay lies nearly flat this morning, its surface warm and slack under a waning gibbous moon still pale in the west. Along the marshy edges of the Thumb shore, joe-pye weed stands at full height, its dusky-rose heads heavy above the sedges. Goldenrod has opened along every field margin and gravel road north toward the AuSable country. Katydids are rasping in the dark hours now, a sound that belongs to August the way ice belongs to January. Trico spinners are due over the river shallows in the early morning calm. Walleye have pulled into the cold depths of the bay's basin. The velvet on white-tail antlers is still intact, but the shedding is three weeks away. Go to the wet ground along any Thumb roadside ditch and count how many stems of joe-pye weed have opened.
